'''Form V''', also known by its two primary disciplines of '''Shien''' and '''Djem So''', as well as '''The Way of the [[Krayt dragon/Legends|Krayt Dragon]]''' or '''The Perseverance Form''', was the fifth of seven forms recognized as canon by the last [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] for [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. It was developed by practitioners of [[Form III/Legends|Form III]] who felt that the defensively minded form unnecessarily extended time spent in combat by forcing its users to wait for an opportunity to strike rather than create their own openings. Form V combat was characterized by power attacks and defense immediately followed by a counterstrike.

Shien, considered the classical variant of Form V, was more adept at blocking [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolts than for blade-to-blade combat, whereas Djem So was developed later and was specifically intended for use in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] combat. Both Shien and Djem So were designed to use an opponent's attack against them, as evidenced by Shien's focus on returning blaster bolts to their origin and Djem So's emphasis on immediate counterattacks. Although some [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] felt that Form V encouraged aggression and domination, that sentiment did not stop many Jedi from practicing the form.

Form V was developed sometime prior to the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], which began in [[3996 BBY]], and it continued to be used for [[Time/Legends|millennia]], during the [[Jedi Civil War]], [[New Sith Wars]], [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and beyond. Like the other lightsaber forms, it saw use among both the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and Jedi. Knowledge of the form survived the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] initiated in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] and into the era of the [[New Jedi Order]]. Practitioners of Form V included [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]], [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]], and [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]].

==Description==
{{Quote|One must question any discipline that has lethal potential. However, if it serves to suppress violent opposition and preserve peace, I believe it is a discipline worth knowing.|Cin Drallig|<ref name="EGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Barrier_of_Blades_SWGTCG_by_Iwanaga.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Rachi Sitra]], a Shien user, creates a [[Telekinesis/Legends#Saber Barrier|lightsaber barrier]]]]
Form V, also known as the Way of the [[Krayt dragon/Legends|Krayt Dragon]], was created by [[Form III/Legends|Form III]] masters who desired a more offensive style, since the defensive nature of Form III often led to prolonged combat, which was potentially dangerous for its practitioners. Form V evolved into an accepted style by combining the defensive maneuvers of Form III with the more aggressive philosophy and tactics of [[Form II/Legends|Form II]]. Form V required a higher level of physical strength than the other [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] forms, due to its focus on complete domination of its practitioners' opponents.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> It was considered the most physically demanding of all the forms.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

The form was developed alongside [[Form IV/Legends|Ataru]] at a [[Time/Legends|time]] when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were increasingly called upon to actively keep the peace.<ref name="EGTTF" /> Some Jedi, noting its dedication to domination and strength, felt that Form V encouraged an inappropriate focus on controlling one's assailants. Other Jedi, including the [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]] [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]], were somewhat ambivalent regarding the form. Nevertheless, the Form's proponents maintained that Form V was an effective and powerful tool for the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="EGTTF" /> Form V had two distinct variations: Shien and Djem So,<ref name="EGTTF" /> and most users had a preference for one or the other.<ref name="TJP" />

===Shien===
{{Quote|You will find it easier to deflect blaster fire with this form&mdash;and it shall also guard you against critical strikes by your opponents.|Zez-Kai Ell|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />}}
The Jedi of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] who developed and employed the classical Form V variant Shien dubbed it the Perseverance Form. Shien was described as being well-adapted to guard against [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire and enemy strikes without compromising one's ability to launch powerful counterattacks. The style worked best when countering attacks from multiple opponents, and was typically less effective against a single adversary. Shien existed at least as early as the [[Jedi Civil War]],<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> which began in [[3959 BBY]].<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> With its focus on repelling blaster fire, Shien kept in mind that Jedi were often outnumbered by their opponents and needed to defend themselves while retaining offensive capability.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> Additionally, there was a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] variant of the form called Sith Shien, though it is not specified how this form might have differed from its Jedi counterpart.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

[[File:SentinelShienExpert_EV_Cristi_Balanescu.png|thumb|right|200px|A female expert of the Shien variant of Form V]]
The Shien opening stance was a high guard position, with the [[Lightsaber hilt/Legends|lightsaber hilt]] held in a two-handed grip above the user's head and the blade angled upward and behind the user. The dominant [[Limb/Legends|leg]] was held back, enabling powerful step-through strikes to be utilized.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> Shien users were also proficient in a maneuver referred to as the "Barrier of Blades," which defended the user from blaster fire and redirected some of the incoming blasts. "Shien Deflection" was another technique familiar to users of that Form V variant, allowing practitioners to simultaneously deflect weapons fire and leap toward an opponent.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> However, Shien was not without its shortcomings&mdash;it was particularly weak against a single opponent.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />

Some users used the reverse Shien grip, an unorthodox variation of Shien where the wielder would hold the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] hilt in a backward position, exposing the front. This grip allowed the user to perform long, sweeping strikes to take down several enemies at a time, whipping the blade forward with the movement of throwing a punch. This variation was rarely seen and, indeed, almost a matter of controversy among lightsaber masters.<ref name="Hero's Guide Web Enhancement #3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030626hero|text=''Hero's Guide'' Web Enhancement #3}}</ref>

===Djem So===
{{Quote|Form V's Djem So variation is devoted specifically to lightsaber dueling.|Cin Drallig|<ref name="EGTTF" />}}
[[File:FallingAvalanche-TPOV.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Dark Jedi utilizing the "Falling Avalanche" attack]]
Djem So was the creation of a group of Form III masters who felt that Soresu was too passive a form. It addressed the shortcomings of Form III, in which a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] could maintain a prolonged defense but was likewise unable to overcome a skilled opponent. Utilizing a combination of blocks and parries, a Djem So user maintained a proper foundation of defense against both ranged and melee attacks. While a Soresu user stayed on the defensive and only counterattacked when necessary or when an opening appeared in the opponent's defense, a Djem So practitioner was not as passive. Immediately after defending against an opponent's strike, a Djem So stylist followed with an attack of their own, bringing the force of the opponent's own blow against them and seeking to dominate the [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|duel]]. Djem So placed a heavy focus on brute strength and pure power, with wide, powerful strikes and parries followed immediately by a counterattack.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" />

Unlike Soresu or Ataru, Djem So required the user not only to counterattack, but also to press the assault, combining [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-enhanced strength with powerful blade combinations to overpower and overwhelm an opponent's defenses. Djem So's sheer power, when combined with physical and Force-imbued strength, was capable of defeating a user of Makashi, a lightsaber form focused on dueling, finesse, and elegance, when employed by a skilled practitioner.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization" />

The Djem So attack stance consisted of holding the lightsaber above the head, angled back and down at an approximately forty-five degree angle.<ref name="Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The characteristic Djem So attack was dubbed the "Falling Avalanche,"<ref name="JATM" /> an overhand power blow that crashed down upon an opponent with exceptional force.<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> Djem So users also employed a tactic known as the "Fluid Riposte," which involved a smooth transition from parrying an attack to a counterstrike.<ref name="JATM" /> Whereas a failing of Shien was its weakness against a single opponent,<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> Djem So was known for having a lack of mobility.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization" />

==Applications==
{{Quote|You will doubtless encounter many situations with multiple assailants. To better protect yourself from blaster fire without compromising your offensive capabilities, use the Shien form.|Kavar|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />}}
[[File:Shien_Deflection_TotC.png|thumb|right|250px|A Rodian Jedi using Shien to deflect blaster fire back at a battle droid]]
Jedi of large stature often chose to use Form V, because it required less agility than other forms of lightsaber combat and made use of their natural strength and reach advantages. It was for this reason that the [[Sith Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]] advised the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Bane]] to learn Djem So. Bane's imposing size and strength served to complement the form; his power attacks were able to knock his opponents back just through sheer kinetic force, throwing them off balance and leaving them vulnerable to further brute-force strikes and power blows that sought not just to penetrate his opponents' defense, but also to push them back and leave them unable to counter blows.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" /> However, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] later commented that all Jedi could enhance their strength with the Force and thus make use of Form V.<ref name="TJP" />

Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] Anakin Skywalker initially employed Shien in his [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|duel]] against the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], although he later employed Form IV while [[Jar'Kai/Legends|wielding]] two blades. Once Dooku managed to [[Sun djem/Legends|destroy]] one of the weapons, Skywalker was forced to revert to his Form V practices.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> While his skill enabled him to hold his own against Dooku, he was unable to overcome the Count's elegant Form II bladework, and was defeated.<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref> The many engagements of the Clone Wars, against both [[Droid/Legends|mechanical]] opponents as well as lightsaber-wielding [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]], honed Skywalker's skills. During his final match against Dooku aboard the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], Skywalker deceived the Sith with a Shien opening stance and Ataru acrobatics, but during the duel he returned to his own preferred Djem So strokes. The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] was barely able to deflect the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight's]] blows and was eventually scorched when his own blade was forced back onto his shoulder. Using Form V, Skywalker pushed Dooku back with powerful blows, bolstered by use of [[Force Enrage|rage]] in the fight, until he eventually disarmed and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the Sith.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization" />

[[File:DarthVader-SWG4.png|thumb|Darth Vader, a master of Form V since his early days as a [[Jedi Knight]], became much stronger after he became a cyborg.|180x180px]]
After turning to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Anakin Skywalker, now known as [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, [[Duel on Mustafar/Legends|dueled]] and was nearly killed by his former Jedi Master, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], on the planet [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization" /> Afterward, Vader employed a new variant of Form V, even more focused on sheer power, in his service to the dark side and [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|quest]] to destroy the Jedi.<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> His defeat on Mustafar and subsequent internment in [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|life-support armor]] forced him to alter his style into a new conglomeration, and he incorporated elements of [[Form VII/Legends|Form VII/Juyo]],<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20080728.html|text=Fightsaber: Mastering the Art of Lightsaber Combat}}</ref><ref name="Secret Weapon">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Secret Weapon]]''</ref> [[Form IV/Legends|Form IV/Ataru]], [[Form III/Legends|Form III/Soresu]],<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader" /> and [[Form II/Legends|Form II/Makashi]] into his fighting style.<ref name="TFU novel">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> Vader again employed Form V on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] against his former master in their [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|final duel]]&mdash;but rather than continuing to fight, Kenobi sacrificed himself.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> Eventually, the same techniques used by Vader against Kenobi were mirrored and used against him by Vader's son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" />

[[File:Shien_Training_DTF.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] utilizing Shien during training]]
In [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]],<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> Luke Skywalker was able to [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|hold his own]] against Darth Vader for a time, despite his minimal [[Jedi training/Legends|training]]. Ultimately, unable to stand against Vader's aggressive barrage, Luke was driven back and disarmed, [[Cho mai/Legends|losing]] his hand. After the duel, he further studied lightsaber skills that he found in a journal left to him by Obi-Wan Kenobi and advanced his abilities.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> Later, aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], Luke was able to [[Battle of Endor/Legends#Demise of the Sith|duel]] Vader on an even footing, mirroring Vader's Form V technique. When Vader attempted to [[Dun Möch/Legends|taunt]] Luke by suggesting that he would tempt Skywalker's [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|sister]] to join the dark side, the tactic provoked the Jedi into a fury, and in that state he was able to defeat the experienced Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]]. Luke responded to his father's aggressive usage with his own furious demonstration of Form V technique, battering Vader down before refusing to continue the fight.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> More than a decade afterwards, he commented that Form V needed to have its aggression and desire to dominate balanced with compassion.<ref name="TJP" />

At times, other weapons beyond standard lightsabers were wielded effectively by Form V practitioners. For example, [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Darth Bane wielded a [[Darth Bane's lightsaber/Legends|curved-hilt lightsaber]]&mdash;a weapon traditionally associated with Form II.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" /> Bane noted that [[Curved-hilt lightsaber/Legends|curved lightsabers]] fit better into the palm, allowing greater power without costing precision. They also altered the angle of attacks slightly, which gave Bane a unique dueling style.<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two" /> Other weapon types wielded by Form V practitioners include [[Lightsaber pike/Legends|lightsaber pikes]], as shown by the Shien practitioner [[Kazdan Paratus]],<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|saberstaffs]], as utilized by the Jedi Master [[Zez-Kai Ell]].<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />

==Practitioners==
{{Quote|Peace through superior firepower.|A Jedi maxim on Form V|<ref name="EGTTF" />}}
[[File:AaylaSecura-JPE.png|thumb|right|225px|Aayla Secura utilizing the Djem So attack stance]]
By the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Form V had been in existence for millennia. The Djem So variant of Form V was developed sometime before [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]],<ref name="NC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and the Jedi Knight Ulic Qel-Droma utilized the form during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]].<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Shien was practiced by Jedi Masters [[Kavar]], Zez-Kai Ell, and [[Vrook Lamar]] during the Jedi Civil War,<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" /> while Ulic Qel-Droma, who lived a few [[Standard year/Legends|decades]] prior to the Jedi Civil War,<ref name="EGTTF" /> favored Djem So.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide" /> The [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]&ndash;era Jedi [[Rojo Trace]] was also versed in Djem So, drawing on his knowledge during a brief bout with Sith Blademaster [[Shak'Weth]].<ref name="RedHarvest">[[Red Harvest (novel)|''Red Harvest'']]</ref> During the [[New Sith Wars]], Form V was mastered by the Sith [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]' Blademaster Kas'im, who [[Sith training|instructed]] numerous apprentices and acolytes in its use, including Darth Bane.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" /> On the Jedi side, [[Battlemaster/Legends|Jedi Battlemaster]] [[Skarch Vaunk]] was also versed in Form V.<ref name="TJP" /> To the Jedi of the Clone Wars era, the most prominent practitioner of Form V was Anakin Skywalker, who mastered both Form V variants.<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith novelization" /> Anakin also felt that any Jedi should be able to use this style, via strength augmentation with the Force if their body was not brawny enough already.<ref name="TJP" />

During the waning years of the Old Republic, Jedi Padawans often spent a year or two studying each Form from II to V.<ref name="EGTTF" /> During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], Obi-Wan Kenobi showed a basic knowledge of Shien, utilizing it in conjunction with the rare reverse grip to skillfully deflect blaster bolts, overcoming Ataru's weakness against blaster-wielding opponents, as he had yet to learn Soresu.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /> [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] was also a practitioner of Form V, as he had mastered all forms of lightsaber combat. Later, during the Clone Wars, Form V practitioners included Jedi Knights [[Khaat Qiyn/Legends|Khaat Qiyn]],<ref name="Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> [[Devan For'deschel]] (Djem So),<ref name="Devan">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20030619devan|text=Devan}}</ref> and [[Zelice Sturm]],<ref name="The Dark Side Beckons">{{LivingForce|Jedi Code: The Dark Side Beckons}}</ref> the Dark Jedi [[Garth Ezzar]]<ref name="Destruction">{{LivingForce|Heart of Evil: Destruction}}</ref> and [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]],<ref name="SoraDatabank">{{DB|character|sorabulq|Bulq, Sora}}</ref> Jedi Masters [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]],<ref name="Revenge of the Sith The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]],<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]],<ref name="TFU novel" /> [[Even Piell/Legends|Even Piell]],<ref name="Jedi Twilight">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]],<ref name="Hero's Guide">''[[Hero's Guide]]''</ref> [[Kazdan Paratus]] (Shien),<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide" /> and [[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]],<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref> and the Padawans [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], who liked to use the reverse Shien grip,<ref name="Clone Wars Campaign [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] and his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] learned Form V from [[Count/Legends|Count]] Dooku during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Labyrinth of Evil" />

[[File:Duel_in_the_Geonosian_Hangar.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Anakin Skywalker utilizing Shien against Count Dooku's Makashi]]
After turning to the dark side and joining the Sith, Vader continued to employ Form V.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> His secret apprentice, [[Galen Marek]], was also familiar with the form, having been personally trained in its usage by Vader.<ref name="TFU novel" /> Vader's son, Luke Skywalker, learned Form V in part by mirroring the swordplay of his father in their first duel, and the younger Skywalker ultimately defeated his father with his use of Form V during their second duel.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> When Luke Skywalker later formed the [[New Jedi Order]], he and the Order learned of the seven combat forms from the book ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'',<ref name="TJP" /> [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] and recordings, particularly the [[Great Holocron/Legends|Great Holocron]], which included a recording by Cin Drallig that explained the lightsaber forms.<ref name="EGTTF" /> One practitioner of the Djem So form in the New Jedi Order was Jedi battlemaster [[Kyle Katarn]].<ref name="LotFPreview5" />

There were considerably fewer practitioners of the controversial horizontal, or "reverse," grip variation of Shien. Around the time of the Clone Wars, Jedi Master [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]]<ref name="JPB">[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'']]</ref><ref name="Hero's Guide Web Enhancement #3" /> and Padawan Ahsoka Tano were two of few Jedi known to actively practice it, though master Gallia favored both grips for her aggressive hybrid blend of Shien and Djem So during the Clone Wars. Ahsoka's master, Anakin Skywalker, even discouraged Tano from using it. Jedi Master [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] occasionally also used Form V with a horizontal grip.<ref name="Hero's Guide" /> The [[Anzat (species)|Anzat]] [[Nikkos Tyris]] also practiced the style,<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref><ref name="Hero's Guide Web Enhancement #3" /> and trained his [[Jensaarai/Legends|followers]] in the form before he [[Duel on Susevfi|died]].<ref name="I, Jensaarai" />

Other Force-users known to employ this rare grip variation were the Jedi Knight turned Sith Lord [[Revan/Legends|Revan]]<ref name="T8:TJCW">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 8: The Jedi Civil War|int=Timeline 8: The Jedi Civil War}}</ref> and Jedi Master [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]],<ref name="Darkness 2">[[Star Wars (1998) 33|''Star Wars'' (1998) 33]]</ref><ref name="Saleucami 1">[[Republic 74|''Republic'' 74]]</ref> as well as Darth Vader's apprentices Galen Marek, [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]] and the [[Dark Apprentice]].

==Behind the scenes==
Form V, along with the other six classical saber forms, was invented by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]] and fencer Jack "Stelen" Bobo for the ''Fightsaber'' part of [[Star Wars Insider 62|''Star Wars Insider'' 62]]. The saber forms were [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] into both the [[original trilogy]] and [[prequel trilogy]] movies up through [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] by assigning practitioners and instances of form usage to the movie characters.<ref name="Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat" /> Since then, numerous [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] sources, including the ''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]'', ''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'', and [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], have further elaborated on the saber forms and the Force-users who employed them.

Form V&mdash;both Shien and Djem So&mdash;appears along the other lightsaber forms in the ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]] as part of the moves and techniques employable by Jedi characters.<ref name="SWG Chapter History 2006">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?id=66843&resource=features|text=Jedi Abilities: Learning the Way}}</ref> Form V also had a non-[[canon]]ical appearance as part of Darth Vader's role in the fighting game ''[[Soulcalibur IV]]'', wherein it comprises part of Vader's fighting style.<ref name="SW.com Fightsaber" /><ref name="Soulcalibur IV">''[[Soulcalibur IV]]''</ref>

It is possible for the player character in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]], to learn Form V from either Kreia or Jedi Masters Kavar, Zez-Kai Ell, or Vrook Lamar after her return from exile. In order to unlock the form, the player must select a character class geared toward lightsaber combat, such as the [[Jedi Guardian/Legends|Jedi Guardian]] or [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinel]] classes. However, it is also possible for the player character to choose the path of [[Jedi Consular]] and learn the [[Force form]]s instead. Form V is the second form unlocked by a lightsaber-focused character and the Exile learns it from either Kreia or the second missing Jedi Master encountered, depending on whether the player took the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] or the dark side path.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />

In ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', Shien is the form of choice for the Vigilance specialization available to Jedi Guardians, as well as the Vengeance specialization available to Sith Juggernauts. Both of those specializations focus on dealing damage over time, boast relatively strong defense and are very effective in combat against multiple opponents, which is canonically an advantage attributed to Shii-Cho. The form itself is only a passive ability and does not cause any visual changes in the fighting style.
